scope: Current-client KismetMathLibrary signed Int32 Add, Subtract and Multiply wrapper arithmetic, simulator wrapping semantics, and repository IR inventory; not full-card or PvP certification.

capture.method: Read-only machine-code capture; live class/function ownership was checked. No function was invoked and no game memory was written. Captures stop at each first RET.

semantics.overflow: The operation is performed in a 32-bit register and the low 32-bit result is written. Signed overflow wraps modulo 2^32 and does not raise an arithmetic exception.

static_ir_inventory.note: Counts describe the repository IR snapshot, include non-PvP assets, and do not establish current-client reachability or current PvP scope.

regression.result: All 18 selected endpoint, overflow, sign and ordinary-value results match the native low-32-bit operation model; the VM reports no faults.
regression.checked_overflow_compilation: The focused BotSim regression also passes with CheckForOverflowUnderflow=true, confirming the explicit unchecked operations preserve wrapping under checked project settings.

implementation.behavior: Add_IntInt, Subtract_IntInt and Multiply_IntInt are now explicitly evaluated in unchecked int32 context so project-wide overflow-check settings cannot change the native wrap behavior.

limitations: The capture establishes the visible parsed-operand arithmetic and result writeback path, not malformed UFunction frames or every property flag.
The BotSim regression tests the local VM; it does not invoke the client executable for differential runtime testing.
Static IR sites do not prove PvP eligibility, execution reachability, or complete card behavior.
Evidence is valid only when the executable SHA-256 matches the value recorded above.
